## Data and cohort

The primary cohort comprises 18 Xenium In Situ sections from 10 head-
and-neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) patients (McCord et al. 2026,
Science Immunology, companion cohort GSE300147/GSE287301), including 7
patients profiled as technical replicates across two independent runs,
and one Ameloblastoma specimen (patient P10) explicitly excluded from
all HNSCC-specific analyses. QC
retained 1,120,780 of 1,186,916 segmented cells across 18 sections
. Patient-specific TCR
probes targeting CDR3 regions enabled direct spatial clonal T-cell
tracking; an empirical false-positive rate (median 0.216) was estimated
from three independent negative controls before any clone call was
trusted.

## Software framework calibration (Q1)

Three spatial null models (constrained permutation, degree-preserving,
graph-preserving) were implemented and calibrated against synthetic
ground truth with known, controllable effect sizes (10 synthetic
patients) before being trusted
on clones. The registered `q1_framework_generalisation` claim -- that
this calibration generalises beyond the primary cohort -- was tested by
applying the identical null-model machinery to an independent,
single-cell-resolution Xenium dataset (Janesick et al. 2023, Nature
Communications, FFPE human breast cancer, CC BY 4.0). All three null
models' Type I error 95% Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals
overlapped the primary cohort's already-established bounds
,
confirming the framework's calibration is not an artefact specific to
the primary cohort's own spatial structure.

## Clone ecological structure (Q2)

A prespecified dual-criterion test (BIC and Tibshirani gap statistic,
required to agree by design) found clone ecological structure to be
continuous, not discrete
. A
three-level nested variance-partition model
(`ecological_structure_score ~ 1 + (1 | patient_id/clone_id)`, n=261
clone-section observations, 158 distinct clones, 10 patients) found all
three variance components non-trivial: patient 29.3% (95% CI 2.7-52.0%),
clone identity 20.2% (95% CI 6.6-36.7%), spatial context 50.4% (95% CI
32.1-75.4%).
This result was robust to clone-size confounding, leave-one-patient-out
resampling (10/10 folds stable), and an independently resegmented
reference subset.

## Barrier topology (Q3)

A prespecified nested mixed model tested whether fibroblast/suppressive-
myeloid barrier topology explains residual variance in clone-tumour
engagement beyond cell-intrinsic state and niche composition (n=152
clone-section rows with a defined barrier fraction). Suppressive-
myeloid barrier fraction significantly predicted lower engagement
(estimate -0.343, 95% CI -0.558 to -0.151, likelihood-ratio test
p=0.0069);
fibroblast barrier fraction was not individually significant. This
finding was direction-concordant with an independent published estimate
(Grout et al. 2022, Cancer Discovery, Pearson r=-0.48 between stromal
alphaSMA density and T-cell infiltration), though this project's raw
bivariate correlation was substantially weaker (r=-0.079) -- the
significant model-adjusted effect only emerges after controlling for
state and niche composition.

## HPV-stratified analysis

Clinical p16 immunohistochemistry status was cross-validated against
Xenium HPV16 E6/E7 oncogene probe signal before any contrast was
defined, surfacing two clinically p16-positive patients with near-zero
molecular signal and one clinically-untested patient with an
unambiguous positive signal. The resulting validated primary contrast (n=4 HPV-positive
vs. n=4 HPV-negative, 2 patients excluded as discordant) was
prospectively shown to require an implausibly large effect size (Cohen's
d>=2.5) for 80% power.
Consistent with this prediction, 0/25 patient-level composition and
ecosystem/structure comparisons reached BH-corrected significance;
leave-one-out and
bootstrap fragility checks nonetheless showed two directionally stable,
exploratory leads (T-cell and Erythroid composition) that this
deliberately capped, small-sample design could not formally confirm.

## External validation summary

Two independent HNSCC reference datasets, distinct from all datasets
used in discovery-phase analyses, were acquired and analysed: GSE139324
(Cillo et al. 2020, Immunity; 26 tumour-infiltrating-lymphocyte samples,
47,801 T cells identified) and TCGA-HNSC (566 bulk RNA-seq samples). All
4 tested T-cell programme gene signatures (cytotoxicity, exhaustion,
proliferation, Treg) showed significant module coherence in GSE139324
(p=0.001 each, exceeding the pre-declared 3/4 success bar). Ecosystem-
derived signatures projected onto TCGA-HNSC showed strong, expected-
direction correlation with an independent immune-infiltration marker
(PTPRC/CD45) for 2/3 pre-specified predictions
. A claim-by-
claim comparison against the source publication's 11 catalogued
findings found 5 reproduced-and-extended, 2 documented divergences, 1
deliberate methodological choice, 1 addressed limitation, and 2 claims
outside this project's data scope
.

## Statistical gatekeeping

Of the 5 prespecified primary claims, 4 passed their pre-declared
success criterion; the HPV contrast did not (by design, not by
contradiction), consistent with its prospective power analysis
(`results/statistical_summary.tsv`).

## Software and data provenance

All analyses were implemented in the `xenium_tcr_ecology` Python/R
package, with a pre-registration and analysis registry tracked in
`governance/analysis_registry.tsv`. Primary results were frozen with
SHA-256 integrity manifests (`data/releases/final_primary/MANIFEST.json`)
before any downstream figure or table generation.
